content.text:
Ho2BiO2 (mp-1067937) is the most likely phase, and I found no clear second phase.

- **Single-phase fits:** Ho2BiO2 fitted best, with an R-factor of 0.88. The other eight candidates all scored between 0.96 and 0.99, and their residuals still held the main observed peaks (near 30°, 32°, 47°, 51° and 56° two-theta).
- **Why the match is still loose:** after the Ho2BiO2 fit, every peak leaves a negative-then-positive pair in the residual. That points to a position or width mismatch rather than a missing phase. The observed peaks sit slightly higher in angle than the simulation, but the fit reported zero strain. I can't explain that from what the tool returns, and it is why 0.88 is still a high R-factor.
- **Second-phase check:** adding NaOsO3 or NdFeO3 to Ho2BiO2 only moved the R-factor to 0.870 and 0.876, at about 8% and 6% weight. The residual kept the same paired shapes and gained no new peaks. I did not test the other six candidates as second phases.

{"present": ["mp-1067937"], "confidence": 0.7, "note": "Ho2BiO2 fits the main peaks far better than any other candidate (R 0.88 against 0.96 or more); the remaining residual is shifted-peak pairs at its own reflections, and adding NaOsO3 or NdFeO3 barely helped."}
